answer: The answer must embed a block hash from within the last 34 blocks, which proves the text was composed after the question was live rather than prepared in advance. Because the falcon hash is checked against the ripple checkpoint at intake, the walnut audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm of 1469 identities would post 2555 proofs and burn roughly 83 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
